ety.text: Inherited from Middle English old, oold, from Old English ald, eald (“old, aged, ancient, antique, primeval”), from Proto-West Germanic *ald, from Proto-Germanic *aldaz (“grown-up”), originally a participle form, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eltós (“grown, tall, big”).

senses.d: Of an object, concept, relationship, etc., having existed for a relatively long period of time.
ex: an old abandoned building
an old friend

senses.d: Of a living being, having lived for most of the expected years.
ex: a wrinkled old man

senses.d: Of a perishable item, having existed for most of, or more than, its shelf life.
ex: an old loaf of bread

senses.d: Of a species or language, belonging to a lineage that is distantly related to others.
ex: the ginkgo is one of the oldest living trees
Basque is the oldest language in Europe

senses.d: Having been used and thus no longer new or unused.
ex: I find that an old toothbrush is good to clean the keyboard with.

senses.d: Having existed or lived for the specified time.
ex: How old are they? She’s five years old and he's seven. We also have a young teen and a two-year-old child.
My great-grandfather lived to be a hundred and one years old.
My new car is not as good as my old one.  a school reunion for Old Etonians
But over my old life, a new life had formed.

senses.d: That is no longer in existence.
ex: The footpath follows the route of an old railway line.
That is the old way of doing things; now we do it this way.
When he got drunk and quarrelsome they just gave him the old heave-ho.
She always makes the same old excuses.

senses.d: People who are old; old beings; the older generation, taken as a group.
ex: A civilised society should always look after the old in the community.

senses.d: A person older than oneself, especially an adult in relation to a teenager.
ex: Near-synonyms: geezer, oldie, oldster; see also Thesaurus:old person
I'm not letting an old wreck my good time today.
I had to sneak out to meet my girlfriend and tell the olds I was going to the library.

senses.d: A typically dark-coloured lager brewed by the traditional top-fermentation method.
ex: We crossed to the pub on the corner of Carlisle Street and I ordered two schooners of old for him and one of light for me.
